en:
The <CLT=cltSTRONG>gold leaf katana<CLT=cltNORMAL> that was
stabbed into Kaede's effigy.

The culprit used that to hit the knob
of the sliding lock to lock the door.

So the <CLT=cltSTRONG>gold leaf<CLT=cltNORMAL> was on the sliding lock
because...

Because when the katana hit the lock,
some of the gold leaf rubbed off on it.

The gold leaf on that katana
did peel rather easily.

Hmmm... That evidence rings a bell.
Specifically, a school bell...

Huh!? Are you talking about a different
school!? What school was it!?

Now now, that doesn't matter anymore.
Let's not dwell on the past.

Oooh, the gold leaf landed on the sliding 
lock when the katana touched it...

So that means, the culprit used the katana 
to move the sliding lock, right?

But wait, how did they move it with a katana?
And from outside Angie's lab?

The clue that might give us the answer
is the <CLT=cltSTRONG>layout of the area<CLT=cltNORMAL> itself.
It was an odd setup, after all.

The katana stabbed into the effigy, the
effigies hung upside down...
Angie didn't do that as part of the ritual?

No... Nowhere in the Necronomicon did
it say you had to hang the effigies.

If it was not part of the ritual...then it must
have been for a different purpose, right?

<CLT=cltMIND>A different purpose...
What could that have been?

<CLT=cltMIND>The culprit somehow used
the setup to lock the room.

<CLT=cltMIND>In that case, I need to know the reason
behind every step of that setup...

<CLT=cltMIND>If I do that, the way the culprit
locked the room should be clear!
